The Escape Pod is a five-ton aerodyne craft measuring 5.3 meters in length and 2.5 meters in diameter. A single liquid hydrogen-fueled thruster provides limited thrust for minor course corrections, capable of up to 3 Gs of acceleration for approximately ninety seconds before fuel is exhausted. Atmospheric reentry relies entirely on heat shielding rather than powered deceleration, and a large steerable para-sail provides limited control of the pod's descent path. The craft carries no landing gear, and touchdown is invariably rough. Injuries during landing are a recognized hazard.

The interior seats four passengers comfortably, with a maximum of six in cramped conditions. Food and life support are rated for approximately twelve days at four occupants, with that window shrinking proportionally as capacity is exceeded. An automatic piloting computer allows the pod to operate without a trained pilot, though these computers were frequently stripped for parts during the resource-scarce Succession Wars, leaving manual controls as the only option aboard many surviving vessels. A distress beacon broadcasts an omnidirectional signal every five minutes for up to thirty days, with later-generation pods programmed to activate automatically two minutes after launch initiation. The signal is detectable within a few hundred kilometers.

The Escape Pod is a ubiquitous emergency craft found aboard virtually every DropShip, JumpShip, and WarShip in known space. First produced in 2647, the five-ton tear-drop-shaped vessel provides crews and passengers with a final means of survival when a stricken vessel cannot be saved. Manufactured by shipyards across the Inner Sphere and Clan space, the pod's core design has changed little since its introduction. Its simplicity and reliability are regarded as its greatest virtues, and nearly every spacefaring culture has maintained production in some form through even the darkest periods of the Succession Wars. The Escape Pod carries no weapons and minimal equipment, yet its combination of limited thrust capability, atmospheric reentry protection, and distress beacon has made it a defining piece of survival hardware across centuries of interstellar travel.

The Escape Pod is fitted as standard equipment aboard virtually every DropShip, JumpShip, and WarShip operated by Inner Sphere powers and Clans alike. Vessels carry pods in numbers proportional to rated crew and passenger complement, with each assigned to a specific boarding station accessible from crew quarters and passenger areas. The design's universal form factor has made it compatible with a wide variety of vessel types without modification. While intended strictly for emergency use, a small number of pods have been adapted with enlarged flight windows for short-range ferry operations between ships and orbital stations, particularly in remote systems where dedicated shuttle assets are unavailable. Operators choosing this role accept a significant reduction in visibility and handling compared to craft designed for the purpose.

The Escape Pod traces its origins to the early Star League era, first appearing in 2647 as a standardized solution to a longstanding problem in space travel. Emergency evacuation procedures prior to its introduction varied widely between manufacturers, and survival rates aboard stricken vessels depended heavily on whatever equipment a particular shipyard chose to install. The standardized design that emerged established dimensions, beacon protocols, and passenger capacity specifications that proved durable enough to outlast the civilization that created them.

The Succession Wars tested the pod's resilience in ways its designers could not have anticipated. As interstellar logistics deteriorated and spare parts grew scarce, automatic piloting computers aboard many pods were stripped out and repurposed, a practical economy that left survivors reliant on manual controls during emergencies. Despite this degradation, the basic design continued to function as intended. The distress beacon's thirty-day broadcast capability saved countless lives in remote systems where rescue might be delayed by weeks or longer.

Production continued across Clan space as well as the Inner Sphere. Clan Jade Falcon manufactured pods at their orbital facility above Sudeten, Clan Ghost Bear produced them on Alshain, and the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora maintained supply for Alliance and Snow Raven vessels. Throughout the Jihad and into the Dark Age, the Escape Pod remained in continuous production, its universal applicability ensuring demand regardless of political upheaval or technological regression. Few pieces of spacefaring equipment can claim the same unbroken record of practical service across more than five centuries of interstellar conflict and recovery.

The Life Boat carries no weapons and cannot re-enter a planetary atmosphere, restricting it to space operations only. Propulsion consists of attitude correction jets that provide basic orientation control but no meaningful thrust. Once deployed, the craft drifts and waits for recovery. Passengers have no ability to maneuver toward help or avoid hazards, and survival depends entirely on the distress beacon being detected and a recovery craft being dispatched.

Life support sustains up to six passengers for 24 to 30 days. Food supplies last approximately 16 days. Power comes from a solar energy collector sail drawn from JumpShip charging sail technology, which continuously recharges the batteries without consuming fuel. This powers lighting, life support, and the distress beacon indefinitely. The beacon's photochemical sail coating also reflects electromagnetic frequencies used by deep-space tracking systems, making the craft highly visible to search operations even without active communication. These two features, passive power and continuous beacon broadcast, define the Life Boat's operational value.

The Life Boat is a five-ton Small Craft built for a single purpose: keeping six people alive long enough to be rescued. Introduced in 2478, it became a fixture aboard JumpShips and DropShips across the Inner Sphere, carried by military and civilian vessels alike. Deliberately simple and inexpensive, it was never intended to fight, maneuver, or operate independently. The design carries enough life support and emergency provisions to sustain its passengers until a recovery vessel can reach them, with a passive power system that keeps the distress beacon broadcasting indefinitely. Its longevity as an essentially unchanged design reflects how little room there is to improve on a craft defined entirely by its constraints.

The Life Boat is standard emergency equipment aboard JumpShips and DropShips throughout the Inner Sphere, carried in launch racks, cargo bays, and docking hardpoints across military and civilian fleets. No faction considers it a combat asset, but its presence reflects its status as essential infrastructure rather than optional equipment. Life Boats are commonly recovered at debris fields following large engagements, found drifting with sails extended and beacons broadcasting, their occupants awaiting retrieval.

The Life Boat entered service in 2478, developed in response to the growing hazards of deep-space travel as interstellar commerce expanded beyond the early colonization waves. Early spacecraft accidents, particularly JumpShip failures in uninhabited systems, exposed the inadequacy of basic life support equipment when rescue could take weeks to arrive. The solar sail power system addressed the central failure of earlier emergency designs, battery depletion, by providing passive, indefinite power to both life support and the distress beacon without any fuel requirement.

The Star League codified Life Boats as mandatory survival equipment aboard registered spacecraft, and production spread across dozens of worlds with no centralized manufacturer. The design's simplicity kept it viable through the Succession Wars, when more sophisticated emergency systems were lost along with the technology to maintain them. It has remained in continuous production ever since, changed only in minor details, across nearly seven centuries of uninterrupted service.

The Kamakiri carries a Tiegart Particle Projection Cannon for reliable long-range direct fire, paired with two Telos ThunderShot Thunderbolt 10 missile launchers that deliver high-damage cluster strikes against armored targets. The combination allows pilots to engage at range with the PPC while using Thunderbolt salvos to threaten heavier opponents, including BattleMechs. A top speed of 118 kilometers per hour gives the design the mobility to strike quickly and disengage before ground forces can respond.

The StarGuard Aurora Reflective armor reflects the DCMS preference for energy-resistant protection, providing improved survival rates against laser and PPC fire. This defensive choice introduces a notable vulnerability to concentrated ballistic and missile fire, requiring pilots to avoid static positions and flak-heavy opponents. The design is best employed in fast attack roles where its speed limits exposure to return fire.

The DAV 155 XL fusion engine powers both the high-speed rotor assembly and the energy weapon systems, but the XL configuration adds structural fragility that experienced pilots account for when taking fire. Overall, the Kamakiri trades baseline armor protection for a combination of speed, firepower, and energy resistance well suited to the mobile strike role it was built to fill.

The Kamakiri Attack VTOL is a 55-ton air assault platform developed by Yan Manufacturing for the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. Introduced in 3100, the design emerged from years of DCMS pressure for a dedicated strike craft capable of supporting combined-arms operations beyond the capabilities of conventional reconnaissance VTOLs. Named for the Japanese praying mantis, the Kamakiri was designed to pair strong direct-fire weaponry with high VTOL speed, offering field commanders a responsive strike asset capable of threatening both armored vehicles and BattleMechs. Yan Manufacturing secured the production contract through an extended Combine procurement process, delivering a platform that has since proven its value across frontier operations in Republic border regions and beyond.

The Shi Kamakiri, or 'death mantis,' is a specialized factory variant operated exclusively within the Ryuken regiments. An improved heavy Gauss rifle replaces the standard Thunderbolt 10 launchers under the centerline, providing significantly greater range and armor penetration against high-value targets. A flight of Shi Kamakiris demonstrated the variant's effectiveness when repulsing a Davion raid on Mokane, accounting for multiple 'Mech kills including an Atlas III. The variant entered production in 3106, six years after the base model.

Yan Manufacturing secured the Kamakiri contract through what company records describe as a prolonged journey through the Combine's procurement bureaucracy. The design team presented its prototype to DCMS representatives just before 3100, and despite the first test flight lasting barely two minutes, procurement officers were sufficiently impressed to extend a long-term production agreement. The New Samarkand facility began full production the same year.

The Kamakiri's first high-profile combat operation came during the Combine's advance on Sakhara V, where a company of the VTOLs was assigned to the Seventh Ghost regiment ahead of the planetary assault. Coordinating with Ghost aerospace fighters, the Kamakiris circled behind the Sakhara Academy Training Battalion's position and fired wave after wave of Thunderbolt strikes into the exposed formation. Despite being outnumbered two-to-one on the ground, the Seventh Ghost overwhelmed the cadets, and the Kamakiris prevented the academy's counter-assault battalion from escaping, leaving fewer than a third of the defenders alive.

The First Arkab Legion took a different approach during the seizure of Ashio, distributing individual Kamakiris among 'Mech lances rather than flying them in concentrated flights. Rather than functioning as dedicated airstrike assets, the embedded VTOLs provided immediate reactive fire during Republic ambushes, with Thunderbolt strikes repeatedly rescuing Arkab warriors from prepared defensive positions. The Legion's MechWarriors began calling the buzzing VTOLs 'little buddies,' reflecting their near-constant presence in lance operations. This embedded-VTOL doctrine has since influenced combined-arms training in several DCMS commands.

The Shun's defining capability is its stealth armor, which allows it to operate in contested airspace where conventional transport VTOLs would draw immediate fire. The system is effective enough for a Shun flight to infiltrate defended areas, deliver up to three squads of battle armor, and withdraw before defenders can mount a coordinated response. A Guardian ECM suite complements the stealth plating, degrading enemy targeting and communications systems in the vicinity and further reducing the risk of detection during the most dangerous phases of an insertion.

Two Mydron Mini Magshot Gauss Rifles give the crew a meaningful self-defense capability, sufficient to discourage pursuit and suppress light ground targets during ingress and egress. TAG designation equipment and a targeting computer extend the Shun's utility beyond pure transport, allowing it to support indirect fire missions by designating targets for artillery and aerospace assets operating in the same battlespace. VTOL mobility allows the Shun to bypass terrain obstacles that would stop conventional transports entirely, making it effective in jungle, urban, and other environments that restrict ground movement.

The design has meaningful limitations. Stealth armor reduces overall payload compared to an unprotected airframe of equivalent mass, and the Shun is not built to absorb sustained punishment. If detection occurs and an adversary brings dedicated anti-aircraft systems to bear, the VTOL's protection quickly becomes inadequate. Mission success depends heavily on crew discipline and thorough pre-mission planning, as much as on the vehicle's technology.

The Shun Transport VTOL takes its name from the Chinese word for shield, a designation that reflects its purpose in Capellan Confederation doctrine. Produced by Tengo Aerospace on Sarna and introduced in 3122, the Shun was developed to provide Confederation ground forces with a capable and survivable platform for delivering battle armor to contested areas. Where earlier transport VTOLs lacked the protection and sophistication to operate effectively in defended airspace, the Shun addressed those deficiencies directly by incorporating advanced stealth technology alongside capable self-defense systems. The design quickly became the preferred battle armor transport in Capellan service, valued for its ability to insert infantry assets into areas that heavier or less capable platforms could not reach, and it has remained a fixture of Confederation combined-arms operations into the ilClan era.

The base Shun serves as the primary battle armor insertion platform in Confederation combined-arms formations. It is typically deployed in pairs or small flights to complicate anti-aircraft targeting, with each aircraft assigned to a specific battle armor unit. Crews and infantry work closely together to develop insertion plans matched to the terrain and defenses of each target. The design excels in jungle, urban, and other environments that restrict conventional ground transport, where VTOL mobility allows it to bypass obstacles entirely. First fielded in 3122, it has seen continuous service on the Capellan-Republic frontier and in the wider conflicts of the mid-Dark Age.

Tengo Aerospace delivered the first Shun Transport VTOLs to Confederation ground forces in 3122, filling a gap in Capellan combined-arms doctrine that had persisted for decades. The Confederation's frontier with the Republic of the Sphere had never been entirely stable, and by the 3120s low-intensity raids and proxy operations using hired mercenaries had become a regular feature of border life. The Shun proved well-suited to this environment, capable of inserting battle armor covertly and supporting operations that required precision rather than mass.

The design's battlefield value was demonstrated on Corey in 3130. When a Republic-sponsored mercenary unit raided the Hollis Industries plant, the Sixth Confederation Reserve Cavalry scrambled a flight of Shuns to intercept before the regiment's heavier elements could respond. Flying low over the jungle canopy, the Shuns delivered battle armor directly onto the raiders' DropShip hull. The battlesuits swiftly overpowered the surprised crew and secured the vessel, ending the incursion before the mercenaries could escape with their stolen equipment.

Not every mission has ended so cleanly. During the CCAF invasion of Demeter in 3144, a Shun flight from the Third Tikonov Guards flew directly into prepared anti-aircraft defenses protecting New Demeter City. Relying solely on stealth to safeguard the flight from detection, the overconfident flight leader ordered the pair straight into heavy defensive coverage. Accurate anti-aircraft fire annihilated both aircraft before the battle armor aboard could be deployed, a costly lesson in the limits of stealth when pilots become overconfident in their equipment.

In other operations, skilled Shun crews demonstrated what the platform could accomplish in experienced hands. During Confederation campaigns into Federated Suns space, pilots assigned to Dynasty Guard formations repeatedly flew through intense defensive fire to deliver their charges against prepared positions. Sang-wei Andrea Hamann of Hamann's Harassers earned a notable reputation during the assault on Taygeta, driving Shun operations deep into Syrtis Fusilier defensive lines to insert battle armor against positions the enemy considered secure. On Corey, Sao-wei Lei Gwok developed unconventional methods during Operation GREAT FLOOD, using creative delivery techniques that kept Republic defenders off-balance across multiple engagements. Their approaches became case studies in how the Shun could be employed beyond the boundaries of standard doctrine.

The Cardinal Transport is powered by a Type 215 XL fusion engine that allows the design to cruise at 86 kph and reach a maximum of 129 kph, delivering the speed appropriate for its assault transport role. The dual-rotor arrangement provides enhanced load stability at the cost of greater pilot workload during low-speed insertion maneuvers, and the ten-ton infantry bay accommodates two Points of Elementals or three squads of Inner Sphere battle armor with full equipment. This transport capacity is the design's primary tactical asset, enabling rapid delivery of armored infantry to contested objectives in environments where ground transport would face unacceptable risk.

The forward-facing armament is modest but effective for a design of this class. A Type OVR-X LB 2-X autocannon provides anti-infantry and light suppression capability, supported by a Type V “Longbow” LRM 5 launcher for standoff engagement. Two Tau-II AP Gauss Rifles give the Cardinal a point-defense capability against battle armor threats, a deliberate design choice given its primary operating environment. All weaponry is concentrated in the forward arc to allow the pilot to bring firepower to bear without repositioning the aircraft.

The Forging AM15 ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a vehicle of this weight class, and the Neil 9000 communications system paired with the RCA Econotrac targeting suite reflects the straightforward, maintainable electronics philosophy that characterizes Trellshire's commercial product line.

The Cardinal Transport is a fifty-ton military VTOL produced by Trellshire Heavy Industries at facilities on Twycross and Itabaiana. Introduced in 3112 to meet the assault transport requirements of Clan Sea Fox and its commercial partners, the Cardinal was designed around a dual-rotor configuration that provides superior load-bearing capacity relative to its weight class. Built to Clan manufacturing standards, the design prioritizes low maintenance overhead and operational reliability, making it well-suited to the extended deployments and disrupted logistics that characterize Dark Age operations. Its ten-ton infantry transport capacity and self-defense armament established the Cardinal as a versatile platform, and its availability through Sea Fox commercial trade networks extended its reach well beyond the Clan space, placing it in service with mercenary commands, Successor State forces, and other buyers seeking capable VTOL assault transport in an era of fractured supply lines.

The Republic Armed Forces variant emerged from a program to expand the Cardinal's infantry capacity for Republic-specific operational requirements. The enlarged twelve-ton infantry compartment allows the variant to carry a full Point of Elementals plus additional support personnel, or larger conventional infantry complements, giving Republic commanders greater flexibility in assault planning. The armament was substantially modified to suit Republic tactical doctrine and supply realities: an MML 5 replaces the original launcher arrangement for flexible short- and long-range indirect fire support, while three small pulse lasers replace the original weapons for improved anti-infantry and point defense performance. This reconfiguration reflects the Republic's preference for organic fire support within individual transport elements rather than reliance on coordinated combined-arms fires. The variant served primarily within Republic Armed Forces formations during the Dark Age, providing assault transport capability in an era when the HPG blackout made centralized logistics increasingly difficult to sustain.

Trellshire Heavy Industries traces its origins to Clan Diamond Shark's aggressive expansion of commercial manufacturing ventures into the Inner Sphere during the late thirty-first and early thirty-second centuries. The company established the Manufacturing Plant SFF-IT1 facility on Itabaiana in 3071, constructing it well clear of the conflicts that devastated the Inner Sphere during the Jihad years. The Itabaiana plant emerged from that era untouched and operating near full capacity, giving Trellshire a significant advantage when the Clan rebranded as Clan Sea Fox and intensified its commercial dealings across the Inner Sphere.

The Twycross facility had a more difficult path. Attacks during the Bloody Tricentennial in the late 3080s destroyed production lines there, requiring extensive reconstruction before the plant could return to operation. By 3112 both sites were producing Cardinals, and the design entered service simultaneously across Sea Fox merchant castes and their primary customers, most especially Clan Jade Falcon, which adopted the Cardinal as a standard assault transport for its infantry-heavy tactical formations. The dual-rotor configuration had undergone years of engineering refinement before the Cardinal reached production, with Trellshire testing multiple rotor arrangements before settling on the final layout that balanced lift capacity against mechanical complexity.

The design spread steadily through the Sea Fox trade network over the following decades, with Galatea emerging as a primary distribution hub from 3136 onward as mercenary demand for capable assault transports grew in the HPG-disrupted Dark Age. Mercenary commands found the Cardinal attractive for its availability through established commercial channels and Trellshire's reputation for reliable parts support. A series of engagements during the 3140s, including intensive use during raiding operations on Galatea in 3141, demonstrated the design's effectiveness in sustained operations and cemented its reputation as a capable and dependable platform. The Republic Armed Forces subsequently developed a re-engineered variant to meet their own operational requirements, further affirming the Cardinal's relevance across a wide range of Inner Sphere and Clan military users.

The Cardinal Transport is powered by a Type 215 XL fusion engine that allows the design to cruise at 86 kph and reach a maximum of 129 kph, delivering the speed appropriate for its assault transport role. The dual-rotor arrangement provides enhanced load stability at the cost of greater pilot workload during low-speed insertion maneuvers, and the ten-ton infantry bay accommodates two Points of Elementals or three squads of Inner Sphere battle armor with full equipment. This transport capacity is the design's primary tactical asset, enabling rapid delivery of armored infantry to contested objectives in environments where ground transport would face unacceptable risk.

The forward-facing armament is modest but effective for a design of this class. A Type OVR-X LB 2-X autocannon provides anti-infantry and light suppression capability, supported by a Type V “Longbow” LRM 5 launcher for standoff engagement. Two Tau-II AP Gauss Rifles give the Cardinal a point-defense capability against battle armor threats, a deliberate design choice given its primary operating environment. All weaponry is concentrated in the forward arc to allow the pilot to bring firepower to bear without repositioning the aircraft.

The Forging AM15 ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for a vehicle of this weight class, and the Neil 9000 communications system paired with the RCA Econotrac targeting suite reflects the straightforward, maintainable electronics philosophy that characterizes Trellshire's commercial product line.

The Cardinal Transport is a fifty-ton military VTOL produced by Trellshire Heavy Industries at facilities on Twycross and Itabaiana. Introduced in 3112 to meet the assault transport requirements of Clan Sea Fox and its commercial partners, the Cardinal was designed around a dual-rotor configuration that provides superior load-bearing capacity relative to its weight class. Built to Clan manufacturing standards, the design prioritizes low maintenance overhead and operational reliability, making it well-suited to the extended deployments and disrupted logistics that characterize Dark Age operations. Its ten-ton infantry transport capacity and self-defense armament established the Cardinal as a versatile platform, and its availability through Sea Fox commercial trade networks extended its reach well beyond the Clan space, placing it in service with mercenary commands, Successor State forces, and other buyers seeking capable VTOL assault transport in an era of fractured supply lines.

The base Cardinal serves primarily as a dedicated assault transport in Clan combined-arms formations, delivering armored infantry directly into contested zones under fire. Clan Sea Fox employs the design throughout its merchant caste operations, using it to support naval infantry deployments and commercial security missions across Inner Sphere and Periphery trade routes. Mercenary commands operating from Galatea and other hiring halls have become significant secondary operators, accessing the Cardinal through Sea Fox commercial networks and benefiting from the parts availability those channels provide. The Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery has adopted the design in limited numbers for assault transport of battle armor units in contested border regions, valuing its speed and transport capacity for rapid infantry insertion. Among Lyran Commonwealth formations, the Third Lyran Guards RCT is a documented operator, typically employing the Cardinal in support of combined-arms assault operations where quick infantry delivery is required.

Trellshire Heavy Industries traces its origins to Clan Diamond Shark's aggressive expansion of commercial manufacturing ventures into the Inner Sphere during the late thirty-first and early thirty-second centuries. The company established the Manufacturing Plant SFF-IT1 facility on Itabaiana in 3071, constructing it well clear of the conflicts that devastated the Inner Sphere during the Jihad years. The Itabaiana plant emerged from that era untouched and operating near full capacity, giving Trellshire a significant advantage when the Clan rebranded as Clan Sea Fox and intensified its commercial dealings across the Inner Sphere.

The Twycross facility had a more difficult path. Attacks during the Bloody Tricentennial in the late 3080s destroyed production lines there, requiring extensive reconstruction before the plant could return to operation. By 3112 both sites were producing Cardinals, and the design entered service simultaneously across Sea Fox merchant castes and their primary customers, most particularly Clan Jade Falcon, which adopted the Cardinal as a standard assault transport for its infantry-heavy tactical formations. The dual-rotor configuration had undergone years of engineering refinement before the Cardinal reached production, with Trellshire testing multiple rotor arrangements before settling on the final layout that balanced lift capacity against mechanical complexity.

The design spread steadily through the Sea Fox trade network over the following decades, with Galatea emerging as a primary distribution hub from 3136 onward as mercenary demand for capable assault transports grew in the HPG-disrupted Dark Age. Mercenary commands found the Cardinal attractive for its availability through established commercial channels and Trellshire's reputation for reliable parts support. A series of engagements during the 3140s, including intensive use during raiding operations on Galatea in 3141, demonstrated the design's effectiveness in sustained operations and cemented its reputation as a capable and dependable platform. The Republic Armed Forces subsequently developed a re-engineered variant to meet their own operational requirements, further affirming the Cardinal's relevance across a wide range of Inner Sphere and Clan military users.

The Shun's defining capability is its stealth armor, which allows it to operate in contested airspace where conventional transport VTOLs would draw immediate fire. The system is effective enough for a Shun flight to infiltrate defended areas, deliver up to three squads of battle armor, and withdraw before defenders can mount a coordinated response. A Guardian ECM suite complements the stealth plating, degrading enemy targeting and communications systems in the vicinity and further reducing the risk of detection during the most dangerous phases of an insertion.

Two Mydron Mini Magshot Gauss Rifles give the crew a meaningful self-defense capability, sufficient to discourage pursuit and suppress light ground targets during ingress and egress. TAG designation equipment and a targeting computer extend the Shun's utility beyond pure transport, allowing it to support indirect fire missions by designating targets for artillery and aerospace assets operating in the same battlespace. VTOL mobility allows the Shun to bypass terrain obstacles that would stop conventional transports entirely, making it effective in jungle, urban, and other environments that restrict ground movement.

The design has meaningful limitations. Stealth armor reduces overall payload compared to an unprotected airframe of equivalent mass, and the Shun is not built to absorb sustained punishment. If detection occurs and an adversary brings dedicated anti-aircraft systems to bear, the VTOL's protection quickly becomes inadequate. Mission success depends heavily on crew discipline and thorough pre-mission planning, as much as on the vehicle's technology.

The Shun Transport VTOL takes its name from the Chinese word for shield, a designation that reflects its purpose in Capellan Confederation doctrine. Produced by Tengo Aerospace on Sarna and introduced in 3122, the Shun was developed to provide Confederation ground forces with a capable and survivable platform for delivering battle armor to contested areas. Where earlier transport VTOLs lacked the protection and sophistication to operate effectively in defended airspace, the Shun addressed those deficiencies directly by incorporating advanced stealth technology alongside capable self-defense systems. The design quickly became the preferred battle armor transport in Capellan service, valued for its ability to insert infantry assets into areas that heavier or less capable platforms could not reach, and it has remained a fixture of Confederation combined-arms operations into the ilClan era.

Introduced in 3142, the Support variant adapts the Shun platform for direct support of battle armor elements already engaged in close combat. Where the standard Shun prioritizes covert infiltration, the Support variant shifts that balance toward enhanced capabilities for battlefield support once insertion is complete. It entered Confederation service on the Republic border alongside base-model Shun flights, complementing standard insertion operations by providing immediate support to infantry units in contact. The variant has been employed in the same operational theaters as the base model throughout the Dark Age and ilClan periods.

Tengo Aerospace delivered the first Shun Transport VTOLs to Confederation ground forces in 3122, filling a gap in Capellan combined-arms doctrine that had persisted for decades. The Confederation's frontier with the Republic of the Sphere had never been entirely stable, and by the 3120s low-intensity raids and proxy operations using hired mercenaries had become a regular feature of border life. The Shun proved well-suited to this environment, capable of inserting battle armor covertly and supporting operations that required precision rather than mass.

The design's battlefield value was demonstrated on Corey in 3130. When a Republic-sponsored mercenary unit raided the Hollis Industries plant, the Sixth Confederation Reserve Cavalry scrambled a flight of Shuns to intercept before the regiment's heavier elements could respond. Flying low over the jungle canopy, the Shuns delivered battle armor directly onto the raiders' DropShip hull. The battlesuits swiftly overpowered the surprised crew and secured the vessel, ending the incursion before the mercenaries could escape with their stolen equipment.

Not every mission has ended so cleanly. During the CCAF invasion of Demeter in 3144, a Shun flight from the Third Tikonov Guards flew directly into prepared anti-aircraft defenses protecting New Demeter City. Relying solely on stealth to safeguard the flight from detection, the overconfident flight leader ordered the pair straight into heavy defensive coverage. Accurate anti-aircraft fire annihilated both aircraft before the battle armor aboard could be deployed, a costly lesson in the limits of stealth when pilots become overconfident in their equipment.

In other operations, skilled Shun crews demonstrated what the platform could accomplish in experienced hands. During Confederation campaigns into Federated Suns space, pilots assigned to Dynasty Guard formations repeatedly flew through intense defensive fire to deliver their charges against prepared positions. Sang-wei Andrea Hamann of Hamann's Harassers earned a notable reputation during the assault on Taygeta, driving Shun operations deep into Syrtis Fusilier defensive lines to insert battle armor against positions the enemy considered secure. On Corey, Sao-wei Lei Gwok developed unconventional methods during Operation GREAT FLOOD, using creative delivery techniques that kept Republic defenders off-balance across multiple engagements. Their approaches became case studies in how the Shun could be employed beyond the boundaries of standard doctrine.

The Garuda's primary weapon is a Series 7N Extended Range Large Laser, mounted on a chin turret that allows it to track targets across a wide arc without requiring the VTOL to orient directly at an opponent. This arrangement is particularly valuable during high-speed lateral passes, where most VTOLs must slow or stop to engage. The laser's extended range allows the Garuda to open fire at distances where enemy countermeasures are less effective.

A Type XV-S Streak LRM 15 launcher provides substantial secondary firepower. The system operates on the same principle as Streak short-range missiles, withholding fire until it can guarantee all missiles will strike their target. Although this limits the launcher to eight rounds of ammunition, the reliability of each salvo makes the system more efficient than a comparable standard LRM arrangement.

A jet booster enables bursts of speed approaching 130 kilometers per hour, a significant capability for a craft carrying this level of armament and protection. Six and a half tons of ferro-fibrous armor places the Garuda among the best-protected VTOLs in active service. An ECM suite degrades enemy sensor-based targeting, and an integrated TAG designator provides artillery spotting capability. These features make the Garuda useful beyond the escort role, though its emphasis on raw combat performance leaves less margin for error than more conservative designs.

Clan Hell's Horses observed with growing interest how Inner Sphere and Clan forces were shifting to VTOLs for battle armor transport. Designs like the Karnov and Cavalry variants offered terrain flexibility that ground transports could not match, but those craft were underarmored and undergunned when left to operate without dedicated escorts. The Horses wanted a VTOL capable of serving as both escort and fire support platform, not merely a cargo carrier. Following negotiations with the Wolves-in-Exile that included an exchange of engineering data, Csesztreg Industriplex Beta began producing the Garuda Heavy VTOL in 3084. The exiled Wolves established a parallel production line at Arc-Royal shortly after. The Garuda was designed to suppress hostile positions while battle armor transports are most vulnerable, and to provide close air support once Elementals have deployed.

The Garuda serves with Clan Hell's Horses and the Wolves-in-Exile as a dedicated escort and fire support asset for VTOL battle armor insertion operations. In the primary doctrinal role, Garudas suppress and soften landing zones while transport VTOLs deliver their Elementals, then swing back to provide close air support after battle armor deploys. The jet booster makes the timing of this sequence practical, allowing the Garuda to protect transports during the vulnerable unloading phase and remain available for follow-on support.

A secondary role uses the Garuda at extended range to provide suppressive fire from the battlefield periphery. Crews assigned to this approach strongly prefer the direct engagement role, and commanders have generally accommodated this preference despite the associated risk. The Garuda is occasionally employed as a general fire support asset independent of battle armor transports, where its combination of speed and armor proves effective, but the primary doctrinal mission remains escort and close air support for Elemental insertion operations.

The Garuda entered production in 3084, the product of a collaboration between Clan Hell's Horses and the Wolves-in-Exile during a period when both Clans were consolidating their Inner Sphere positions following the Jihad. The engineering exchange that produced the design reflected the pragmatic working relationships that had developed between Crusader and Warden factions through years of shared occupation zone experience, relationships that would have been unthinkable a generation earlier.

Production began at Csesztreg Industriplex Beta, a facility that had passed through multiple political owners across the Succession Wars and Clan Invasion eras. By the time the Garuda program launched, Clan Hell's Horses had established firm control of Csesztreg and were investing in its industrial base. The Arc-Royal production line at WC Site 4 gave the Wolves-in-Exile both an independent supply line and a stake in the design's continued development, ensuring the Garuda would remain available to both partners regardless of the political relationship between them.

In service, the Garuda developed a reputation as a platform that crews consistently flew more aggressively than doctrine recommended. The preferred approach of making direct passes against targets rather than providing support from the battlefield edge has resulted in elevated casualty rates for Garuda crews, but the combat performance data from those engagements proved difficult for commanders to argue against. The distinctive silhouette of a Garuda alongside VTOL transports became a recognizable indicator of incoming Elemental deployment in both Hell's Horses and Wolves-in-Exile tactical operations.

Both production lines remained active through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with the design continuing to serve its original purpose alongside successive generations of VTOL transport variants.

The Karnov's airframe is built around the DAV 190 ICE aircraft engine, a powerplant known for reliability and ruggedness. Drive shafts extend from the central wing spar down wing pylons to twin rotor assemblies capable of a full ninety-degree tilt, allowing horizontal speeds exceeding 180 kilometers per hour. The speed comes at a cost, as the large rotor blades must be locked vertical for landing. Many inexperienced pilots have wrecked both aircraft and crew by forgetting this critical step. Variable-geometry landing gear allows the Karnov to straddle loads up to 3.3 meters tall, with the internal cargo bay ramp extending fully for drive-on loading and unloading.

StarSlab armor forged specifically for the Karnov provides reasonable protection against infantry weapons and light shrapnel, though the oversized rotors remain vulnerable to any sustained fire. Many crashed Karnovs can be found on battlefields with fuselage and wing struts intact but rotors completely shot away. The base Karnov carries no weapons and no dedicated targeting system, relying entirely on speed and standoff distance for protection. A Johnston Q-Rotor communications system handles coordination with ground units, and the six-ton cargo bay accommodates a range of mission loads from bulk supplies to light vehicles.

The Karnov UR Transport is a heavy-lift tilt-rotor VTOL whose origins remain one of the enduring mysteries of Inner Sphere military logistics. Although distributed by the New Earth Trading Company since at least the early Succession Wars, NETC has never possessed VTOL manufacturing facilities of its own, and no other firm has publicly claimed credit for the design's production. Despite this uncertainty, the Karnov has earned a reputation for reliability and ruggedness that few transport craft can match. The tilt-rotor configuration makes it one of the fastest VTOLs of its weight class, equally capable as a cargo carrier and a flying crane. Military forces, mercenary commands, and commercial operators across every Successor State employ the Karnov for supply, logistics, and battlefield recovery missions, making its distinctive silhouette synonymous with rear-area transport operations throughout the Inner Sphere.

A custom forty-five ton conversion first observed in 3082, significantly larger than the standard thirty-ton Karnov. Protected by four tons of vehicle stealth armor powered by an Angel ECM suite, the Heavy Stealth variant carries an 85-rated XL fusion engine augmented by a VTOL jet booster for sprint insertions and extractions. Sponson-mounted machine guns provide suppressive fire as troops deploy from the four-ton infantry bay, while a fourteen-ton cargo bay holds the proceeds of smash-and-grab raids. A criminal organization calling itself "The Master's Chosen" operated at least four of these modified Karnovs as a bandit fleet, conducting raids across Republic territory. Republic security forces downed one during an attack on Epsilon Indi in December 3083, though stripped serial numbers and a thorough memory wipe of the onboard computers hampered efforts to identify the aircraft's origin.

The Karnov UR Transport entered widespread Inner Sphere distribution around 2920, when the New Earth Trading Company began offering the design through its extensive commercial network. Unknown to most buyers, NETC's entire supply came from ComStar, provided as part of a secret arrangement in exchange for food, resources, and intelligence. ComStar maintained Karnov production lines on Terra, drawing on manufacturing expertise and engineering records preserved from the Star League era, and shipped completed vehicles to NETC for resale. This arrangement continued for over a century, providing both parties with what they needed while keeping the Karnov's true manufacturing origins hidden.

The revelation of the Com Guards following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 disrupted this arrangement. ComStar retained an increasing share of Karnov production for its own expanding military forces, sharply reducing shipments to NETC. The bloodied but unbowed Com Guards made clear to NETC that the priority of all available resources was rebuilding their divisions back to strength, and the resulting supply shortage forced NETC to take an unprecedented step. As a consolation, Precentor Martial Focht granted NETC a free license to produce the Karnov on their own, leading to the construction of one of the most recently built manufacturing facilities in the Inner Sphere on New Earth. The factory produced several hundred customized units annually, fulfilling both military and civilian orders.

NETC's policy of customization ensured that Karnov variants became as widely varied as the operators who purchased them. The 3055 Upgrade was the first factory variant, addressing long-standing complaints about the lack of defensive armament and the dangerously sensitive rotor system. Battle armor transport, Periphery strike, and other specialized configurations followed as demand and technology evolved. Meanwhile, the original Terran production line passed from ComStar to Word of Blake control, and then to the Republic of the Sphere following the liberation of Terra. The Republic invested heavily in advanced variants incorporating stealth technology, viewing rapid battle armor insertion as a critical capability for its combined-arms forces.
